grades.rationale: The aggregate report preserves rule codes (E501, unresolved-import) and per-tool counts; tools that produce line numbers (ruff, ty) ran with status=ok so raw output would be traceable, though the YAML itself lists no line ranges.

Severity distributions are well-calibrated: bandit.by_severity all zero, pip_audit.by_severity all zero, ruff.by_category.security=0, with the only findings being correctness (E501) and a typing error — no inflation.

All lenses covered with status=ok (ruff, ty, bandit, radon, complexipy, vulture, pip-audit, detect-secrets) except mypy which is not_installed; ty covers the typing lens so coverage is effectively complete but mypy's absence is unexplained.
Every count is derivable from a tool with status=ok, and the report clearly distinguishes mypy.status=not_installed from the other tools' ok status, avoiding phantom counts.
Per rubric adaptation, graded 2 by default; by_rule entries like ruff E501 and ty unresolved-import do pin fix direction implicitly via rule codes.

Findings cite specific rule codes (ruff E501, ty unresolved-import), and clean passes are evidenced by structural counts proving the tools scanned real code (radon.cc.total_functions=1, complexipy.total_functions=1, bandit ran with version 1.8.6 yielding zero).

Full complexity telemetry present: radon.cc.max=2 with over_threshold_10=0, complexipy.max=2 with over_threshold_15=0, radon.mi.min=61.68 with under_20=0, and halstead.max_volume=27.0 — thresholds and measured numbers all recorded.
Report is purely numeric/structural with no editorializing, as the adaptation note anticipates.

Clean distributions are richly documented: radon.cc.distribution {A:1}, radon.mi.distribution {A:1}, detect_secrets.new_since_baseline=0, pip_audit.vulnerabilities=0, and bandit.total=0 cross-agreeing with ruff.by_category.security=0.
